# Finding the Number of Sylow Bases for G

## Setting Up the Sylow Base

For |G| = 60 = 2² · 3 · 5, a Sylow (Hall) base is a set {H₂, H₃, H₅} where each Hₚ is a Hall {p′}-subgroup:

| Subgroup | Description | Order |
|----------|------------|-------|
| H₂ = ⟨a⟩ | Hall {3,5} | 15 |
| H₃ = ⟨a³, b⟩ | Hall {2,5} | 20 |
| H₅ = ⟨a⁵, b⟩ | Hall {2,3} | 12 |

## Computing the Conjugation Action

Since ⟨a⟩ ⊴ G with |⟨a⟩| = 15, the quotient G/⟨a⟩ has order 4. I compute:

$$b a b^{-1} = (1\;3\;2)(4\;6\;8\;5\;7) = a^2$$

This confirms b induces the automorphism a ↦ a² on ⟨a⟩ ≅ ℤ/15, which has order 4 (since 2⁴ ≡ 1 mod 15).

## Finding N_G(B)

Since all three subgroups have distinct orders (15, 20, 12), normalizing the base B requires normalizing each Hₚ individually:

$$N_G(B) = N_G(H_2) \cap N_G(H_3) \cap N_G(H_5)$$

**H₂:** Since ⟨a⟩ ⊴ G, we have N_G(H₂) = G.
